event.title: Flavio Bolsonaro Officially Launches Presidential Campaign in Brazil
event.canonical_title: Flavio Bolsonaro Officially Launches Presidential Campaign in Brazil
event.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro, a Brazilian senator and son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has officially launched his presidential campaign to challenge incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in the upcoming October elections. He received endorsements from Argentine President Javier Milei and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, along with a message from his jailed father.

timeline.title: Brazil Recalls Ambassador After Milei's Insults to Lula
timeline.summary: Brazil has recalled its ambassador to Argentina following remarks made by President Javier Milei, who referred to Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva as a 'convict' and a 'thief.' The comments were made during an event supporting Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential campaign, where Milei warned of a 'Lula risk' posed by leftist candidates. The recall is a diplomatic response to what Brazil termed 'insults' directed at its leader.

event_overview.title: About Brazil Elections
event_overview.subject: Brazil Elections
event_overview.summary: Brazil’s 2026 general elections will choose the country’s president and vice president alongside governors, senators, and federal and state or district legislators. The presidential contest is a nationwide direct election administered by Brazil’s Electoral Justice, with a second round if no ticket wins an absolute majority of valid votes in the first round.

facts.label: Election dates
facts.value: The first round is scheduled for October 4, 2026; a second round, where required, is scheduled for October 25, 2026.

facts.label: Offices being elected
facts.value: Voters will elect the president and vice president, state and Federal District governors and vice governors, senators, federal deputies, and state or district deputies; two Senate seats are being contested in each state and the Federal District in this cycle.

facts.label: Electoral system for president
facts.value: The president and vice president run as a single ticket. A ticket must receive an absolute majority of valid votes to win in the first round; otherwise, the two leading tickets proceed to a runoff.

facts.label: Candidate selection and registration
facts.value: Political parties and federations may hold conventions from July 20 through August 5, 2026 to choose candidates and decide coalitions. A public campaign launch is distinct from the formal registration process; presidential and vice-presidential registration requests are decided by the Superior Electoral Court (TSE).

facts.label: Election administration
facts.value: The Superior Electoral Court’s 2026 rules govern preparation, voting, vote counting, tabulation, certification of winners, and post-election procedures for the general election.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline follows specific developments involving a presidential campaign and Brazil–Argentina diplomatic tensions, rather than providing a complete record of candidates, court rulings, polling, campaign activity, or election results.
